prompt: Players fall through the platforms. Fix it by putting the platforms on collision layer 2 and adding layer 2 to the player's collision mask, with movement done in _physics_process.

config.plan_model: Agent-tool model parameter 'sonnet' (Claude Code sub-agent; the harness did not report the resolved model id)
config.how: one fresh general-purpose sub-agent per plan, reads a job file with project brief + the developer prompt, writes numbered plan (<=8 steps, no code) via Write; not Claude Code plan mode

plans.text:
1. Open level_01.tscn and the TileMapLayer's physics settings to confirm how the platforms currently collide and which collision layer and mask they use. Check that the tileset actually has a physics layer with collision polygons on the platform tiles, since missing shapes are a common cause of falling through.
2. Set the TileMapLayer's collision layer to layer 2 (and clear it from other layers unless ground still needs layer 1). Decide whether the ground and platforms share the TileMapLayer or need separate ones, and keep the ground's layer assignment consistent with that decision.
3. Open the Player's CharacterBody2D collision settings and add layer 2 to its collision mask, keeping any existing mask bits (such as ground) enabled. Leave the Player's own collision layer unchanged.
4. Review player.gd and confirm all movement, gravity, and the move-and-slide call happen in _physics_process rather than _process. If any movement or velocity logic sits in _process, move it into _physics_process and use the physics delta.
5. Check the two enemy scenes for masks that should also include layer 2, so enemies do not fall through the platforms either. Update them only if they walk on those platforms.
6. Verify the Player's CollisionShape2D is enabled, correctly sized, and positioned, and that no one-way or disabled-shape settings on the platform tiles undermine the fix.
7. Run level_01.tscn and test landing on, walking along, and jumping through platforms at various speeds, including fast falls, to check for tunnelling. Confirm enemies and ground still behave correctly.
8. Summarize the changes made (layer and mask settings, any movement relocation) and flag anything that did not match expectations, such as additional layers or scenes that needed adjusting.

1. Open level_01.tscn and the TileMapLayer node, and confirm that the platform tiles currently have a physics layer defined in the TileSet with collision shapes painted on the platform tiles. Note the layer and mask values the ground and platforms currently use.
2. In the TileSet's physics layer settings, set the collision layer for the platforms to layer 2 (leave the mask as needed), making sure the platform tiles actually have collision polygons assigned.
3. If the ground and platforms live on separate TileMapLayer nodes, apply the layer 2 setting to the platform layer only, so the ground keeps its existing layer.
4. Select the Player CharacterBody2D and open its Collision section. Keep its current layer, and add layer 2 to its collision mask so it detects the platforms alongside whatever it already collides with.
5. Open player.gd and check where movement and gravity are applied. Move all of that logic, including velocity changes and the move_and_slide call, into _physics_process, and remove any duplicate movement from _process.
6. Check that the Player's CollisionShape2D has a valid shape that is sized and positioned correctly over the sprite, and that it is not disabled.
7. Check the two enemy scenes and any other bodies for masks that should also include layer 2, so enemies do not fall through the platforms either.
8. Run level_01.tscn and test landing, walking, and jumping on the platforms, on both the ground and the elevated platforms. Confirm the player no longer falls through, and that the enemies still behave correctly.

1. Open level_01.tscn and the TileMapLayer node, and confirm which tiles make up the platforms versus the ground. Note the current physics layer and collision settings on the tileset.
2. In the TileSet resource, make sure a physics layer exists and that the platform tiles have collision polygons painted on them, since missing polygons are a common cause of falling through.
3. Set the TileMapLayer's physics layer to collision layer 2 only, so the platforms live on layer 2. If ground and platforms share one TileMapLayer, decide whether to split them so ground keeps its current layer.
4. Select the Player CharacterBody2D and add layer 2 to its collision mask, keeping any layers it already collides with. Leave the player's own collision layer unchanged.
5. Open player.gd and check that gravity and movement (velocity updates and move_and_slide) run inside _physics_process rather than _process. Move them there if they are elsewhere.
6. Check the two enemy scenes and any other bodies that should stand on platforms, and add layer 2 to their masks if they also need to collide with platforms.
7. Run level_01.tscn and verify the player lands on and walks across the platforms without falling through, including edges and jumps. Turn on visible collision shapes to confirm the layers line up.
8. Report back what was changed (layers, masks, script location) and any side effects found, such as enemies or other objects now colliding differently.

2. Set the TileMapLayer's collision layer to layer 2 for the platform tiles, making sure the tileset's physics layer actually has collision polygons on the platform tiles.

1. Open level_01.tscn and the TileMapLayer for the ground and platforms, and confirm how the platform tiles currently get their physics shapes and which collision layer they sit on. This establishes why the player passes through them.
2. In the TileMapLayer's tileset, make sure every platform tile has a physics layer with a collision polygon defined, since tiles without shapes cannot collide regardless of layer settings.
3. Set the platforms' TileMapLayer collision layer to layer 2 only, leaving the ground's layer assignment as the developer intends, and check the second enemy scene and the first for any reliance on the old layer.
4. Open the Player scene and add layer 2 to the CharacterBody2D's collision mask while keeping the existing mask bits, so the player still collides with whatever it already hit.
5. Open player.gd and verify that all movement and move_and_slide calls happen in _physics_process rather than _process, moving any gravity or velocity handling there if it is elsewhere.
6. Check that the CollisionShape2D on the Player is enabled, has a sensible shape and size, and is not disabled or offset away from the sprite.
7. Review the two enemy scenes' collision masks and layers to make sure the layer 2 change does not make enemies unintentionally collide with, or pass through, the platforms.
8. Run level_01.tscn and test walking, jumping and landing on every platform and the ground, then confirm enemies and the player behave correctly and nothing falls through.

1. Open level_01.tscn and the TileMapLayer's TileSet to confirm which physics layer the platform tiles currently use and whether the tiles actually have collision polygons defined.
2. Set the platform tiles' collision to layer 2 in the TileSet's physics layer settings (and the TileMapLayer's collision settings), keeping the ground on its existing layer unless it should also move.
3. Select the Player's CharacterBody2D and add layer 2 to its collision mask while keeping its existing mask bits, so it still collides with the ground and enemies.
4. Open player.gd and check where movement and move_and_slide are currently called, and whether gravity and velocity are applied there.
5. Move all movement, gravity, and move_and_slide logic into _physics_process, removing any duplicate handling from _process so physics runs at a fixed step.
6. Check the two enemy scenes and any other bodies to confirm their masks still match the layers they need to hit, so the layer change does not break them.
7. Run level_01.tscn and test landing on, walking along, and jumping through platforms from several heights to confirm the player no longer falls through.
8. Review the result for edge cases such as tile seams, one-way platform settings, and fast falls, and adjust only if a regression appears.

1. Open level_01.tscn and the TileMapLayer's TileSet to confirm how the platform tiles currently have physics shapes and which collision layer they sit on. Also check player.gd and the Player's current collision layer and mask to understand why the player passes through.
2. In the TileSet's physics layer settings, set the platform tiles' collision layer to layer 2 only, so ground and platforms are identifiable as a distinct layer. Make sure each platform tile actually has a collision polygon painted so there is something to collide with.
3. Select the Player's CharacterBody2D and add layer 2 to its collision mask, keeping any existing mask bits (such as the ground layer) intact. Leave the player's own collision layer unchanged unless it conflicts.
4. Review the two enemy scenes and any other bodies that should stand on platforms, and decide whether their masks also need layer 2. Change only what is needed so enemy behaviour is not altered unintentionally.
5. Open player.gd and check where movement and gravity are applied, moving that logic into _physics_process if it is currently in _process. Make sure the movement call used there is the standard body-movement method so collisions are resolved each physics frame.
6. Verify the CollisionShape2D on the player is enabled, sized sensibly, and not disabled or offset in a way that would let it clip through thin platforms. Also confirm the TileMapLayer's physics is enabled in its properties.
7. Run level_01.tscn and test landing on, walking along, and jumping onto the platforms, including the thinnest ones and the edges. Confirm that enemies still collide as expected.
8. If anything still falls through, turn on visible collision shapes in the debug menu to inspect the layers and masks at runtime, and adjust accordingly. Save the scenes once the behaviour is correct.

1. Open level_01.tscn and the TileMapLayer's TileSet to confirm which physics layer the platform tiles use and whether the tiles actually have collision polygons defined. This establishes the current cause of the fall-through before changing anything.
2. In the TileSet's physics layer settings, set the collision layer to layer 2 for the ground and platform tiles. Leave the collision mask on the tiles as it is unless the enemies need it.
3. Select the Player's CharacterBody2D and add layer 2 to its collision mask, keeping its existing mask bits so it still collides with whatever it hits now. Leave the player's own collision layer unchanged.
4. Open player.gd and check where movement and gravity are applied. Move all velocity and gravity updates, along with the move_and_slide call, into _physics_process, and remove any movement logic from _process.
5. Check that the Player's CollisionShape2D has a shape assigned and a sensible size, and that it is not disabled. A missing or tiny shape would cause fall-through no matter what the layers are.
6. Check the two enemy scenes and any other bodies that should stand on platforms. Add layer 2 to their masks if they are meant to collide with the platforms, so the layer change doesn't leave them falling through.
7. Run level_01.tscn and test landing on the ground, landing on and jumping onto the platforms, and walking along platform edges. Confirm the player no longer falls through and that movement feels the same at different frame rates.
8. Check that nothing else relied on the old layer assignments, such as raycasts, Area2D triggers or hazards. Adjust their masks if they stopped detecting the platforms.
